title: Count Nodes in a Linked List
statement:
You are given the head of a singly linked list. Count the number of nodes in the list and print that count. An empty list has `0` nodes.

The list is given in the input as its length followed by its node values in order from head to tail. Your function receives only the `head` node (or `null` when the list is empty) and must count the nodes by walking the list.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`, the number of nodes.
If `n > 0`, the second line contains `n` space-separated integers: the node values from head to tail.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the number of nodes in the list.

examples.explanation: Walking from the head visits the nodes holding 10, 20, 30 and 40, which is 4 nodes.
The list is empty, so the head is null and there are no nodes to count.
Equal values are still separate nodes, so all 3 are counted.

hints: Start a pointer at the head and a counter at 0.
While the pointer is not null, increase the counter and move the pointer to its next node.
Handle the empty list: if head is null the loop never runs and the answer is 0.
